properties.areaDesc: Kimble, TX; Mason, TX; Menard, TX
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 9 at 9:07AM CST until November 9 at 3:00PM CST by NWS San Angelo TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Kimble County in west central Texas...
Western Mason County in west central Texas...
Southeastern Menard County in west central Texas...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM CST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Some low-water crossings may become
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 901 AM CST, the public reported heavy rain in low water
crossings. This will cause small stream flooding. Between 2.5 and
3.5 inches of rain have fallen over the past 2-3 days.
- Low water crossings are the most likely place to experience minor
flooding. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are
expected over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
South Llano River State Park, US-377 near Telegraph, Ranch Road
2291 north of I-10, Ranch Road 385 from US-377 to US-290, Farm to
Market 2169 near Junction, The Intersection Of Us-83 And Ranch
Road 1773, and Us-83 Near The Kerr-Kimble County Line
- This includes Interstate 10 between Mile Markers 435 and 477.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 3 PM CST THIS AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: La Salle, TX; McMullen, TX; Webb, TX
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 9 at 9:03AM CST until November 9 at 11:00AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
At 903 AM CST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 3
and 4 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1
inch are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Southeastern La Salle, Southern McMullen and
Northeastern Webb Counties.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: Anchorage Hillside / Eagle River
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 9 at 5:15AM AKST until November 10 at 3:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations
between 2 and 8 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze.
Winds gusting as high as 60 mph, mainly across southern parts of
the Anchorage Hillside.

* WHERE...Anchorage Hillside / Eagle River.

* WHEN...From noon today to 3 PM AKST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Monday evening and Tuesday morning commutes. Strong
winds could cause damage to trees and power lines.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong storm system moving across the Gulf
of Alaska will bring a mix of snow, freezing rain and rain to much
of the Anchorage Hillside and Eagle River between this afternoon
and early Tuesday afternoon.  Precipitation will start as mainly
heavy snow this afternoon, then transition to a mix of snow and
freezing rain tonight to early Tuesday morning as east winds begin
to pick up. Precipitation could transition to plain rain by Tuesday
morning as temperatures rise above freezing.  Uncertainty for the
timing of precipitation type transition remains high, with a later
transition to rain and freezing rain potentially leading to higher
snowfall totals. If warmer air moves in quicker, expect less snow
and ice accumulation.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.headline: Blizzard Warning issued November 9 at 5:15AM AKST until November 10 at 12:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions likely. Total snow accumulations between
8 and 16 inches. Winds could gust as high as 45 mph. Visibility
reduced to as low as one quarter mile in blowing snow.

* WHERE...Thompson Pass.

* WHEN...From 11 AM this morning to noon AKST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Visibility could be
significantly reduced within heavy snow.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A band of light to moderate snow is expected
late this morning before tapering off in the afternoon. A second
round of heavier snow is likely this evening through Tuesday
morning. Conditions will begin to improve starting late Tuesday
morning as winds begin to slowly diminish and snow becomes lighter
and more showery in nature.
properties.instruction:
A Blizzard Warning means severe winter weather conditions are
expected or occurring. Falling and blowing snow with strong winds and
poor visibilities are likely. This will lead to whiteout conditions,
making travel very hazardous. If you must travel, have a winter
survival kit with you. If you get stranded, stay with your vehicle.

For the latest road conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...North-facing beaches of Puerto Rico, including Culebra.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Lingering northerly swells generated by
distant surface low over the central Atlantic will support
breaking waves of 5 to 8 feet and a high risk of life-
threatening rip currents along the northern exposed beaches of
Puerto Rico and Culebra.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 9 at 5:06AM PST until November 10 at 10:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to locally moderate coastal flooding expected.
Additionally, dangerous rip currents and surf of 3 to 7 feet
expected along west-facing beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon PST Tuesday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of parking lots and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming conditions
due to elevated surf and strong rip currents.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest tides will occur in the morning
each day, peaking at 7.2-7.4 feet today, which is 1.2 to 1.4
feet above astronomical tide predictions. Higher surf today
could prolong coastal impacts.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water to avoid
hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 9 at 6:46AM CST until November 14 at 12:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Los Olmos Creek Near Falfurrias affecting Brooks County.

.Excessive rainfall is forecast to continue upstream of Los Olmos
into early this week, leading to a rise in river levels that may
approach action stage late tonight.

For the Los Olmos Creek...including Falfurrias...elevated river
levels are forecast.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Los Olmos Creek near Falfurrias.

* WHEN...Until late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding reaches 120 feet wide
into flood plain-persons vulnerable to lowland flooding should move
equipment to higher ground

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:15 AM CST Monday the stage was 1.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 6.9 feet
early Wednesday morning.
- Action stage is 5.0 feet. The river is expected to reach action
stage late tonight.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 700 PM CST.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp and Windy Pass.

properties.areaDesc: Dalton Highway Summits; White Mountains and High Terrain South of the Yukon River
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 9 at 3:33AM AKST until November 10 at 6:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow and blowing snow expected. Total snow accumulations up
to one inch. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...Dalton, Elliott, and Steese Highway Summits.

* WHEN...From 3 PM this afternoon to 6 PM AKST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Areas of blowing snow could
reduce visibility below one half mile at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Light snow will continue throughout the day
Monday with gusts up to around 25 mph. East/northeast winds will
increase later today into tonight and Tuesday, with light
additional snow expected.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 9 at 6:05AM CST until November 9 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM CST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even

direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 8 at 7:50PM PST until November 9 at 10:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.6 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 12 to 16 ft expected.

* WHERE...San Francisco.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 10:35
AM Monday 11/9, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 11:04 AM
Tuesday 11/10, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 11:35 AM
Wednesday 11/11, 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 12:10 PM
Thursday 11/12, 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.4 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 8 at 12:52PM PST until November 10 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding during morning high tides expected. For the High Surf
Advisory, dangerous rip currents and large breaking waves of 5
to 7 feet, except peaking at 6 to 9 feet on Monday.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Flooded sandy beach areas and moderate beach
erosion possible. Localized and shallow flooding of beach
parking lots, bike paths, and walkways. Isolated damage is
unlikely, but cannot be discounted.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of 7.2 to 7.6 feet (MLLW) are
expected each morning. Surf and coastal flooding impacts peak
on Monday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 8 at 12:52PM PST until November 10 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 10 to 16 feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of 7.1 to 7.4 feet (MLLW) are
expected each morning. The High Surf and Coastal Flood
Advisories may need to be extended through the week.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 8 at 12:52PM PST until November 10 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to
elevated surf up to 4 to 6 feet expected. Minor tidal overflow
possible during morning high tides, especially across west
facing beaches.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa
Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide
at beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with normal tidal
ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is also possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of 7.2 to 7.6 feet (MLLW) are
expected each morning.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 7 at 10:23PM EST until November 10 at 2:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Beaches of Volusia, Indian River, Saint Lucie, Martin,
and Brevard Counties.

* WHEN...Through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
